units.literal: The emperor alighted from the carriage weeping; that evening he lodged in Ying’s camp.

units.zh: 穎府有九錫之儀，陳留王送貂蟬文衣鶡尾，明日，乃備法駕幸于鄴，唯豫章王熾、司徒王戎、僕射荀藩從。
units.en: Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-bestowal regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.
units.literal: Ying’s headquarters held the regalia for the nine bestowals; the Prince of Chenliu presented sable-cicada insignia, patterned robes, and pheasant-tail pennants; the next day the full imperial equipage was prepared and proceeded to Ye; only Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Minister Wang Rong, and Vice Director Xun Fan accompanied.

units.zh: 庚申，大赦，改元爲建武。
units.en: The reign was renamed Jianwu on gengshen amid another general amnesty.
units.literal: On the gengshen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jianwu.

units.zh: 八月戊辰，穎殺東安王繇。
units.en: Prince Yao of Dong’an was executed by Prince Ying on wuchen in the eighth month.
units.literal: On the wuchen day of the eighth month Ying killed Prince Yao of Dong’an.

units.zh: 張方復入洛陽，廢皇后羊氏及皇太子覃。
units.en: Zhang Fang returned to Luoyang and stripped the empress and crown prince of their titles once more.
units.literal: Zhang Fang again entered Luoyang and deposed Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan.

units.zh: 匈奴左賢王劉元海反於離石，自號大單于。
units.en: Liu Yuan, the Xiongnu worthy king of the left who is known as Yuanhai, rose at Lishi and proclaimed himself great chanyu.
units.literal: The Xiongnu Worthy King of the Left Liu Yuan (Yuanhai) rebelled at Lishi and styled himself great chanyu.

units.zh: 安北將軍王浚遣烏丸騎攻成都王穎于鄴，大敗之。
units.en: Wang Jun, general who pacifies the north, hurled Wuhuan horse against Prince Ying at Ye and shattered his army.
units.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun sent Wuhuan cavalry against Prince Ying of Chengdu at Ye and greatly defeated him.

units.zh: 穎與帝單車走洛陽，服御分散，倉卒上下無齎，侍中黃門被囊中齎私錢三千，詔貸用。
units.en: Prince Ying and the emperor bolted toward Luoyang in one cart, servants and luggage lost along the way; court eunuchs lent three thousand cash from their belts under emergency warrant.
units.literal: Ying and the emperor fled in a single carriage toward Luoyang; attendants and baggage were scattered; in haste high and low had no provisions; palace attendants and yellow gates carried three thousand cash of private money in satchels, and an edict authorized borrowing it.

units.zh: 所在買飯以供，宮人止食于道中客舍。
units.en: They bought meals from wayside kitchens, and the palace ladies slept in posting houses.
units.literal: Wherever they stopped they bought rice to supply him; palace women ate only at roadside inns.

units.zh: 宮人有持升餘糠米飯及燥蒜鹽豉以進帝，帝噉之，御中黃門布被。
units.en: One maid offered a bowl of gritty rice with dried garlic and salted beans; he ate it and slept under a eunuch’s quilt.
units.literal: A palace woman brought more than a sheng of coarse rice, dried garlic, salted beans, and fermented black beans for the emperor; the emperor ate them; he used a eunuch’s cotton quilt.

units.zh: 次獲嘉，市粗米飯，盛以瓦盆，帝噉兩盂。
units.en: At Huojia he bought two bowls of rough rice from a street vendor in a clay dish.
units.literal: Halting at Huojia, they bought coarse rice in the market, served in an earthen bowl; the emperor ate two bowls.

units.zh: 有老父獻蒸雞，帝受之。
units.en: An old man presented a steamed chicken, which the emperor accepted.
units.literal: An old man presented a steamed chicken, and the emperor accepted it.

units.zh: 至溫，將謁陵，帝喪履，納從者之履，下拜流涕，左右皆歔欷。
units.en: At Wen, intending to worship at the tombs, he lost his shoes, borrowed a guard’s pair, and wept so bitterly that every retainer wept with him.
units.literal: When they reached Wen, about to visit the mausoleum, the emperor lost his shoes, put on a follower’s footwear, descended to bow with streaming tears, and those at his side sobbed.

units.zh: 及濟河，張方帥騎三千，以陽燧青蓋車奉迎。
units.en: Zhang Fang met him mid-river with three thousand riders and a chariot hung with a bronze fire mirror and blue canopy.
units.literal: When they crossed the river, Zhang Fang led three thousand horsemen to welcome him with a sun-mirror canopy carriage.

units.zh: 方拜謁，帝躬止之。
units.en: Zhang Fang kowtowed, but the emperor raised him with his own hands.
units.literal: Fang bowed in audience; the emperor in person stopped him.

units.zh: 辛巳，大赦，賞從者各有差。
units.en: A general amnesty on xinsi came with graded rewards for everyone who had stayed with the throne.
units.literal: On the xinsi day a general amnesty was proclaimed; followers were rewarded each according to grade.

units.zh: 冬十一月乙未，方請帝謁廟，因劫帝幸長安。
units.en: Zhang Fang asked leave to escort the sovereign to the shrines on yiwei in the eleventh month, then hijacked the court and marched west to Chang’an.
units.literal: On the yiwei day of winter’s eleventh month Fang requested the emperor to visit the temple, then seized the emperor and forced him to go to Chang’an.

units.zh: 方以所乘車入殿中，帝馳避後園竹中。
units.en: Zhang Fang rammed his own coach into the throne hall while the emperor fled into the rear bamboo copse.
units.literal: Fang drove the carriage he rode into the palace hall; the emperor galloped to hide in the bamboo grove of the rear garden.

units.zh: 方逼帝升車，左右中黃門鼓吹十二人步從，唯中書監盧志侍側。
units.en: He was forced into the carriage with twelve marching musicians and only Lu Zhi at his elbow.
units.literal: Fang forced the emperor to mount the carriage; twelve yellow-gate musicians from the left and right followed on foot; only Director of the Secretariat Lu Zhi attended at his side.

units.zh: 方以帝幸其壘，帝令方具車載宮人寶物，軍人因妻略後宮，分爭府藏。
units.en: With the emperor under his roof, Zhang Fang was told to ready wagons for concubines and imperial treasure; his men then abducted palace women and tore the vaults apart in a scramble for loot.
units.literal: Because the emperor lodged in Fang’s camp, the emperor ordered Fang to prepare carts to convey palace women and treasures; the soldiers thereupon took women from the rear palace as wives and separately struggled over the plunder of the treasuries.

units.zh: 魏晉已來之積，掃地無遺矣。
units.en: Generations of hoarded wealth from Wei and Western Jin vanished overnight.
units.literal: The accumulations since Wei and Jin were swept away without remainder.

units.zh: 行次新安，寒甚，帝墮馬傷足，尚書高光進面衣，帝嘉之。
units.en: At Xin’an it was bitterly cold; the emperor fell from a horse and injured his foot; Secretariat official Gao Guang presented a face-cloth, and the emperor praised him.
units.literal: Marching, they halted at Xin’an; it was bitterly cold; the emperor fell from a horse and injured his foot; Minister of the Household Gao Guang presented a face-cloth; the emperor praised him.

units.zh: 河間王顒帥官屬步騎三萬，迎于霸上。
units.en: Prince Yong rode to Bashang with thirty thousand men to greet the column.
units.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian led thirty thousand foot and horse of his staff to welcome him at Bashang.

units.zh: 顒前拜謁，帝下車止之。
units.en: Prince Yong knelt in the road, but the emperor stepped down to raise him.
units.literal: Yong stepped forward to bow in audience; the emperor alighted from the carriage and stopped him.

units.zh: 以征西府爲宮。
units.en: The prince’s western headquarters became the temporary palace.
units.literal: The western expedition headquarters was made the palace.

units.zh: 唯僕射荀藩、司隸劉暾、太常鄭球、河南尹周馥與其遺官在洛陽，爲留臺，承制行事，號爲東西臺焉。
units.en: Vice director Xun Fan, metropolitan superintendent Liu Tun, minister of ceremonies Zheng Qiu, and Henan intendant Zhou Fu stayed in Luoyang with the remnant bureaucracy, acting in the emperor’s name as the paired “east and west” headquarters.
units.literal: Only Vice Director Xun Fan, Metropolitan Superintendent Liu Tun, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Qiu, and Henan Intendant Zhou Fu, with the surviving officials at Luoyang, formed a rear headquarters, acting on edict, called the eastern and western bureaus.

units.zh: 丙午，留臺大赦，改元復爲永安。
units.en: The Luoyang remnant proclaimed amnesty on bingwu and restored the reign title Yongan.
units.literal: On the bingwu day the rear headquarters proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name back to Yongan.

units.zh: 辛丑，復皇后羊氏。
units.en: Empress Yang was reinstated on xinchou.
units.literal: On the xinchou day Empress Yang was restored.

units.zh: 李雄僭號成都王，劉元海僭號漢王。
units.en: Li Xiong styled himself prince of Chengdu at his stronghold, while Liu Yuan called himself prince of Han.
units.literal: Li Xiong usurped the title Prince of Chengdu; Liu Yuan usurped the title Prince of Han.

units.zh: 十二月丁亥，詔曰：「天禍晉邦，冢嗣莫繼。
units.en: On the dinghai day in the twelfth month an edict began: “Heaven scourges Jin, and no son of mine survives to succeed.
units.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month an edict stated: “Heaven has punished the Jin state; no heir succeeds.

units.zh: 成都王穎自在儲貳，政績虧損，四海失望，不可承重，其以王還第。
units.en: Prince Ying proved unfit while heir apparent and has forfeited the trust of the realm, so he must be stripped of the succession and sent home to his fief.
units.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu, while heir, failed in government; within the four seas hope was disappointed; he cannot bear the heavy charge; let him return to his residence as a prince.

units.zh: 豫章王熾先帝愛子，令問日新，四海注意，今以爲皇太弟，以隆我晉邦。
units.en: Prince Chi of Yuzhang, the late emperor’s favorite, grows in reputation every day, and he shall be named imperial younger brother and heir to steady the house of Jin.
units.literal: Prince Chi of Yuzhang was the late emperor’s beloved son; his fair fame grows daily; within the four seas all eyes turn to him; now let him be made imperial younger brother and heir to uplift our Jin state.

units.zh: 以司空越爲太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朕躬。
units.en: Minister of Works Prince Yue is appointed grand tutor to work beside Grand Steward Yong in guiding the throne.
units.literal: Let Minister of Works Yue be made grand tutor, together with Grand Steward Yong to flank and assist my person.

units.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
units.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
units.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.

units.zh: 安南將軍虓、安北將軍浚、平北將軍騰各守本鎮。
units.en: Generals Xiao, Jun, and Teng are ordered to hold their existing commands.
units.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Xiao, General Who Pacifies the North Jun, and General Who Pacifies the North Teng each guard their original garrisons.

units.zh: 高密王簡爲鎮南將軍，領司隸校尉，權鎮洛陽；
units.en: Prince Jian of Gaomi becomes general who guards the south and acting metropolitan superintendent at Luoyang.
units.literal: Prince Jian of Gaomi is made general who guards the south, concurrently metropolitan superintendent, acting in authority at Luoyang;

units.zh: 東中郎將模爲寧北將軍、都督冀州，鎮于鄴；
units.en: Sima Mo moves to general who guards the north with Ji Province command, based at Ye.
units.literal: General of the Household Gentlemen of the East Mo is made general who guards the north and area commander for Ji Province, stationed at Ye;

units.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘領荊州，以鎮南土。
units.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief who guards the south, keeps order in Jing Province.
units.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South Liu Hong holds Jing Province to secure the south.

units.zh: 周馥、繆胤各還本部，百官皆復職。
units.en: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin go back to their posts, and every minister returns to duty.
units.literal: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin each return to their original commands; the hundred officials all resume their posts.

units.zh: 齊王冏前應還第，長沙王乂輕陷重刑，封其子紹爲樂平縣王，以奉其嗣。
units.en: Prince Jiong ought long ago to have been sent to his domain, and Prince Yi suffered a cruel death, so enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping to preserve his line.
units.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi should earlier have returned to his residence; Prince Yi of Changsha was lightly subjected to heavy punishment; enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping county to continue his line.

units.zh: 自頃戎車屢征，勞費人力，供御之物皆減三分之二，戶調田租三分減一。
units.en: Because armies have marched again and again, palace supplies are cut by two-thirds, and the poll tax and land rent are each reduced by a third.
units.literal: Recently war-chariots have repeatedly marched, exhausting men and resources; articles for the imperial household are all reduced by two-thirds; household levies and field rent are each reduced by one-third.

units.zh: 蠲除苛政，愛人務本。
units.en: Harsh statutes are swept away so the people may return to their fields.
units.literal: Harsh government is remitted; the people are cherished and the root is sought.

units.zh: 清通之後，當還東京。」
units.en: Once peace is restored, the court will return to Luoyang.”
units.literal: After the realm is cleared and at peace, we shall return to the eastern capital.”

units.zh: 大赦，改元。
units.en: The edict ended with a general amnesty and a new reign title.
units.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.

units.zh: 以河間王顒都督中外諸軍事。
units.en: Prince Yong of Hejian received overall command of every army.
units.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made area commander for all military affairs within and without.

units.zh: 二年春正月甲午朔，帝在長安。
units.en: On the new moon of the first month of the second year the sovereign still sat at Chang’an.
units.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on the jiawu new moon, the emperor was at Chang’an.

units.zh: 夏四月，詔封樂平王紹爲齊王。
units.en: An edict in the fourth month restored the Qi princedom for Prince Shao of Leping.
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month, an edict enfeoffed Prince Shao of Leping as prince of Qi.

units.zh: 丙子，張方廢皇后羊氏。
units.en: Zhang Fang stripped Empress Yang of her title again on bingzi.
units.literal: On the bingzi day Zhang Fang deposed Empress Yang.

units.zh: 六月甲子，侍中、司徒、安豐侯王戎薨。
units.en: On jiazi in the sixth month, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.
units.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.

units.zh: 隴西太守韓稚攻秦州刺史張輔，殺之。
units.en: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked and killed Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou.
units.literal: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou, and killed him.

units.zh: 李雄僭即帝位，國號蜀。
units.en: Li Xiong usurped the imperial title and named his state Shu.
units.literal: Li Xiong usurped the imperial position and named his state Shu.

units.zh: 秋七月甲午，尚書諸曹火，燒崇禮闥。
units.en: Secretariat offices caught fire on jiawu in the seventh month and consumed the Chongli gate.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiawu day, fire broke out in the secretariat bureaus and burned the Chongli gate-tower.

units.zh: 東海王越嚴兵徐方，將西迎大駕。
units.en: Prince Yue of Donghai massed troops in Xu, preparing to march west and escort the emperor home.
units.literal: Prince Yue of Donghai drilled troops in the Xu region, intending to march west and welcome the great chariot.

units.zh: 成都王穎部將公師藩等聚眾攻陷郡縣，害陽平太守李志、汲郡太守張延等，轉攻鄴，平昌公模遣將軍趙驤擊破之。
units.en: Gongshi Fan and other officers of Prince Ying of Chengdu gathered a host, stormed commanderies, killed Yangping Prefect Li Zhi and Ji Prefect Zhang Yan, and turned to attack Ye until Duke Mo of Pingchang’s general Zhao Xiang defeated them.
units.literal: Subordinates of Prince Ying of Chengdu such as Gongshi Fan gathered a host, stormed commanderies and prefectures, killed Yangping Prefect Li Zhi, Ji Prefect Zhang Yan, and others, then turned to attack Ye; Duke Mo of Pingchang sent General Zhao Xiang to defeat them.

units.zh: 八月辛丑，大赦。
units.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed on xinchou in the eighth month.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on the xinchou day, a general amnesty.

units.zh: 驃騎將軍、范陽王虓逐冀州刺史李義。
units.en: Prince Xiao of Fanyang, general of agile cavalry, expelled Prefect Li Yi from Ji.
units.literal: General of Agile Cavalry, Prince Xiao of Fanyang, drove out Ji Prefect Li Yi.

units.zh: 揚州刺史曹武殺丹楊太守朱建。
units.en: Cao Wu, inspector of Yangzhou, executed Zhu Jian, prefect of Danyang.
units.literal: Yangzhou Inspector Cao Wu killed Danyang Prefect Zhu Jian.

units.zh: 李雄遣其將李驤寇漢安。
units.en: Li Xiong sent Li Xiang to raid Han’an.
units.literal: Li Xiong sent his general Li Xiang to raid Han’an.

units.zh: 車騎大將軍劉弘逐平南將軍、彭城王釋于宛。
units.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief of chariots and cavalry, drove Prince Shi of Pengcheng from Wan.
units.literal: General-in-chief of Chariots and Cavalry Liu Hong drove General Who Pacifies the South, Prince Shi of Pengcheng, from Wan.

units.zh: 九月庚寅朔，公師藩又害平原太守王景、清河太守馮熊。
units.en: On the gengyin new moon Gongshi Fan killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
units.literal: On the gengyin new moon of the ninth month, Gongshi Fan again killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.

units.zh: 庚子，豫州刺史劉喬攻范陽王虓於許昌，敗之。
units.en: Liu Qiao defeated Prince Xiao at Xuchang on gengzi.
units.literal: On the gengzi day, Yu Prefect Liu Qiao attacked Prince Xiao of Fanyang at Xuchang and defeated him.

units.zh: 壬子，以成都王穎爲鎮軍大將軍、都督河北諸軍事，鎮鄴。
units.en: On renzi Prince Ying was named general who stabilizes the army, given Hebei command, and ordered to Ye.
units.literal: On the renzi day, Prince Ying of Chengdu was made general who stabilizes the army and area commander for Hebei military affairs, garrisoned at Ye.

units.zh: 河間王顒遣將軍呂朗屯洛陽。
units.en: Prince Yong posted Lü Lang in Luoyang.
units.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian dispatched General Lü Lang to encamp at Luoyang.

units.zh: 冬十月丙子，詔曰：「得豫州刺史劉喬檄，稱潁川太守劉輿迫脅驃騎將軍虓，距逆詔令，造構凶逆，擅劫郡縣，合聚兵眾，擅用苟晞爲兗州，斷截王命。
units.en: On bingzi in the tenth month an edict read: “A memorial from Yu Prefecture Inspector Liu Qiao has arrived, accusing Yingchuan Prefect Liu Yu of coercing Prince Xiao, defying the throne, raising troops, and installing Gou Xi at Yanzhou.
units.literal: On the bingzi day of winter’s tenth month an edict stated: “I have received the proclamation of Yu Prefect Liu Qiao, which says that Yingchuan Prefect Liu Yu has coerced General of Agile Cavalry Xiao, resisted edicts, contrived rebellion, seized commanderies on his own authority, massed troops, and arbitrarily appointed Gou Xi to Yanzhou, cutting off imperial commands.

units.zh: 鎮南大將軍、荊州刺史劉弘，平南將軍、彭城王釋等，其各勒所統，徑會許昌，與喬并力。
units.en: Liu Hong, Prince Shi, and the rest were ordered to march on Xuchang with Liu Qiao.
units.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South, Jingzhou Inspector Liu Hong, General Who Pacifies the South, Prince Shi of Pengcheng, and others—each shall lead his command and proceed directly to Xuchang to join forces with Qiao.

units.zh: 今遣右將軍張方爲大都督，統精卒十萬，建武將軍呂朗、廣武將軍騫貙、建威將車刁默等爲軍前鋒，共會許昌，除輿兄弟。」
units.en: Zhang Fang was named supreme commander at the head of one hundred thousand men, with Lü Lang, Qian Chu, and Diao Mo among his van, to join the Xuchang operation against Liu Yu and his kin.”
units.literal: Now the right general Zhang Fang is sent as supreme commander, leading one hundred thousand picked troops, with General Who Establishes Martiality Lü Lang, General of Broad Martiality Qian Chu, General Who Establishes Might Diao Mo, and others as the vanguard, to meet together at Xuchang and remove Yu and his brothers.

units.zh: 丁丑，使前車騎將軍石超；
units.en: On the dingchou day, the former General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Chao was dispatched;
units.literal: On the dingchou day, dispatch former General of Chariots and Cavalry Shi Chao;

units.zh: 北中郎將王闡討輿等。
units.en: General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household Wang Chan was to strike Liu Yu and the others.
units.literal: General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household Wang Chan shall attack Yu and the others.

units.zh: 赤氣見于北方，東西竟天。
units.en: Crimson aurora stretched across the northern sky from east to west.
units.literal: Red vapors appeared in the north, stretching from east to west across the sky.

units.zh: 有星孛于北斗。
units.en: A comet brushed the Northern Dipper.
units.literal: There was a broom star at the Northern Dipper.

units.zh: 平昌公模遣將軍宋冑等屯河橋。
units.en: Duke Mo posted Song Zhou at the Yellow River bridge.
units.literal: Duke Mo of Pingchang sent General Song Zhou and others to encamp at the River Bridge.

units.zh: 十一月，立節將軍周權詐被檄，自稱平西將軍，復皇后羊氏。
units.en: Zhou Quan faked orders, called himself general who pacifies the west, and briefly restored Empress Yang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, General Who Establishes Integrity Zhou Quan forged a summons, styled himself general who pacifies the west, and restored Empress Yang.

units.zh: 洛陽令何喬攻權，殺之，復廢皇后。
units.en: Prefect He Qiao killed Zhou Quan and deposed the empress again.
units.literal: Luoyang Prefect He Qiao attacked Quan, killed him, and again deposed the empress.

units.zh: 十二月，呂朗等東屯滎陽，成都王穎進據洛陽，張方、劉弘等並桉兵不能禦。
units.en: Lü Lang held Xingyang while Prince Ying took Luoyang; Zhang Fang and Liu Hong would not engage.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Lü Lang and others encamped east at Xingyang; Prince Ying of Chengdu advanced and occupied Luoyang; Zhang Fang, Liu Hong, and others all held their troops and could not resist.

units.zh: 范陽王虓濟自官渡，拔滎陽，斬石超；
units.en: Prince Xiao crossed at Guandu, took Xingyang, and slew Shi Chao;
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Fanyang crossed from Guandu, captured Xingyang, and beheaded Shi Chao;

units.zh: 襲許昌，破劉喬于蕭，喬奔南陽。
units.en: then struck Xuchang, routed Liu Qiao at Xiao, and drove him to Nanyang.
units.literal: he raided Xuchang, defeated Liu Qiao at Xiao, and Qiao fled to Nanyang.

units.zh: 右將軍陳敏舉兵反，自號楚公。
units.en: Chen Min of the right guards rebelled and proclaimed himself duke of Chu.
units.literal: General of the Right Chen Min raised troops in rebellion and styled himself duke of Chu.

units.zh: 矯稱被中詔，從沔漢奉迎天子，逐揚州刺史劉機、丹楊太守王曠。
units.en: He forged a palace order to escort the emperor from the Han and Mian valleys and ousted Liu Ji and Wang Kuang.
units.literal: He falsely claimed to bear a secret edict from the palace to welcome the Son of Heaven from the Han and Mian rivers, expelled Yangzhou Inspector Liu Ji, and Danyang Prefect Wang Kuang.

units.zh: 遣弟恢南略江州，刺史應邈奔弋陽。
units.en: His brother Hui raided Jiangzhou and put Inspector Ying Miao to flight toward Yiyang.
units.literal: He sent his younger brother Hui south to raid Jiang Province; Inspector Ying Miao fled to Yiyang.

units.zh: 光熙元年春正月戊子朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: On the wuzi new moon of the first month of spring in Guangxi 1, there was a solar eclipse.
units.literal: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Guangxi, on the wuzi new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 帝在長安。
units.en: The emperor was in Chang’an.
units.literal: The emperor was in Chang’an.

units.zh: 河間王顒聞劉喬破，大懼，遂殺張方，請和于東海王越，越不聽。
units.en: When Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, heard that Liu Qiao had been defeated, he was terrified. He killed Zhang Fang and sought peace with Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, but Yue refused.
units.literal: Yong, Prince of Hejian, heard that Liu Qiao had been defeated and was greatly afraid; he then killed Zhang Fang and requested peace from Yue, Prince of Donghai, but Yue did not listen.

units.zh: 宋冑等破穎將樓裒，進逼洛陽，穎奔長安。
units.en: Song Zhou and the others defeated Ying’s general Lou Pou and pressed on toward Luoyang, forcing Ying to flee to Chang’an.
units.literal: Song Zhou and others defeated Ying’s general Lou Pou, advanced to threaten Luoyang, and Ying fled to Chang’an.

units.zh: 甲子，越遣其將祁弘、宋冑、司馬纂等迎帝。
units.en: On jiazi Prince Yue sent Qi Hong, Song Zhou, and Sima Zuan to escort the emperor.
units.literal: On the jiazi day Yue dispatched his generals Qi Hong, Song Zhou, Sima Zuan, and others to welcome the emperor.

units.zh: 三月，東萊㡉令劉柏根反，自稱㡉公，襲臨淄，高密王簡奔聊城。
units.en: In the third month Liu Baigen, magistrate of Jiao County in Donglai, rebelled as “Lord of Jiao,” seized Linzi, and drove Prince Jian of Gaomi to Liaocheng.
units.literal: In the third month, Liu Baigen, magistrate of Jiao in Donglai, rebelled, styled himself Lord of Jiao, raided Linzi, and Prince Jian of Gaomi fled to Liaocheng.

units.zh: 王浚遣將討柏根，斬之。
units.en: Wang Jun’s general destroyed Liu Baigen.
units.literal: Wang Jun sent a general to campaign against Baigen and beheaded him.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，東海王越屯于溫。
units.en: Prince Yue encamped at Wen on jisi in the fourth month.
units.literal: In summer, on the jisi day of the fourth month, Prince Yue of Donghai encamped at Wen.

units.zh: 顒遣弘農太守彭隨、北地太守刁默距祁弘等于湖。
units.en: Prince Yong sent Hongnong Prefect Peng Sui and Beidi Prefect Diao Mo to block Qi Hong and the others at Hu.
units.literal: Yong dispatched Hongnong Prefect Peng Sui and Beidi Prefect Diao Mo to block Qi Hong and the others at Hu.

units.zh: 五月，枉矢西南流。
units.en: A “crooked-arrow” meteor streaked southwest in the fifth month.
units.literal: In the fifth month a crooked-arrow meteor flew southwest.

units.zh: 范陽國地燃，可以爨。
units.en: Soil in Fanyang smoldered hot enough to cook food.
units.literal: In the Fanyang princedom the earth caught fire and could be used for cooking.

units.zh: 壬辰，祁弘等與刁默戰，默大敗，顒、穎走南山，奔于宛。
units.en: On renchen Qi Hong and the others battled Diao Mo; Mo was greatly defeated; Princes Yong and Ying fled to the southern mountains and ran to Wan.
units.literal: On the renchen day Qi Hong and others battled Diao Mo; Mo was greatly defeated; Yong and Ying fled to the southern mountains and ran to Wan.

units.zh: 弘等所部鮮卑大掠長安，殺二萬餘人。
units.en: Qi Hong’s Xianbei troopers sacked Chang’an and killed more than twenty thousand.
units.literal: The Xianbei under Qi Hong’s command greatly plundered Chang’an and killed more than twenty thousand persons.

units.zh: 是日，日光四散，赤如血。
units.en: That day the sun’s light scattered blood-red in every quarter.
units.literal: That day sunlight scattered in four directions, red as blood.

units.zh: 甲午又如之。
units.en: The same crimson light returned on jiawu.
units.literal: On the jiawu day it was again so.

units.zh: 己亥，弘等奉帝還洛陽，帝乘牛車，行宮藉草，公卿跋涉。
units.en: On jihai Qi Hong convoyed the emperor to Luoyang in an ox-cart on straw bedding while nobles walked.
units.literal: On the jihai day Hong and others escorted the emperor back to Luoyang; the emperor rode an ox-cart; the traveling palace used straw mats; dukes and ministers trudged on foot.

units.zh: 戊申，驃騎、范陽王虓殺司隸校尉邢喬。
units.en: Prince Xiao executed Metropolitan Commandant Xing Qiao on wushen.
units.literal: On the wushen day General of Agile Cavalry, Prince Xiao of Fanyang, killed Metropolitan Commandant Xing Qiao.

units.zh: 己酉，盜取太廟金匱及策文各四。
units.en: Thieves stole four gold caskets and four patent bundles from the Grand Temple on jiyou.
units.literal: On the jiyou day thieves stole four golden caskets from the Grand Temple and four document bundles.

units.zh: 六月丙辰朔，至自長安，升舊殿，哀感流涕。
units.en: On the sixth month’s new moon he returned from Chang’an, entered the old hall, and wept.
units.literal: On the bingchen new moon of the sixth month, he arrived from Chang’an, ascended the old hall, and wept in grief.

units.zh: 謁于太廟。
units.en: He worshiped at the Grand Temple.
units.literal: He visited the Grand Temple.

units.zh: 復皇后羊氏。
units.en: Empress Yang was restored again.
units.literal: Empress Yang was restored.

units.zh: 辛未，大赦，改元。
units.en: Xinwei brought a general amnesty and a new reign title.
units.literal: On the xinwei day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

units.zh: 秋七月乙酉朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: A solar eclipse fell on the yiyou new moon of the seventh month.
units.literal: In autumn, on the yiyou new moon of the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

units.zh: 太廟吏賈苞盜太廟靈衣及劍，伏誅。
units.en: Jia Bao was executed for stealing ritual robes and swords from the temple.
units.literal: Temple clerk Jia Bao stole spirit garments and swords from the Grand Temple and was executed.

units.zh: 八月，以太傅、東海王越錄尚書，驃騎將軍、范陽王虓爲司空。
units.en: In the eighth month Prince Yue took the secretariat and Prince Xiao became minister of works.
units.literal: In the eighth month, Grand Tutor Prince Yue of Donghai was ordered to record secretariat affairs; General of Agile Cavalry, Prince Xiao of Fanyang, was made minister of works.

units.zh: 九月，頓丘太守馮嵩執成都王穎，送之于鄴。
units.en: Feng Song of Dunqiu captured Prince Ying and sent him to Ye.
units.literal: In the ninth month, Dunqiu Prefect Feng Song seized Prince Ying of Chengdu and sent him to Ye.

units.zh: 進東嬴公騰爵爲東燕王，平昌公模爲南陽王。
units.en: Sima Teng became prince of Dongyan and Sima Mo prince of Nanyang.
units.literal: Duke Teng of Dongying was advanced in rank to prince of Dongyan; Duke Mo of Pingchang was made prince of Nanyang.

units.zh: 冬十月，司空、范陽王虓薨。
units.en: Prince Xiao of Fanyang, minister of works, died in the tenth month.
units.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister of Works, Prince Xiao of Fanyang, died.

units.zh: 虓長史劉輿害成都王穎。
units.en: Liu Yu, Prince Xiao’s chief clerk, killed Prince Ying.
units.literal: Xiao’s chief clerk Liu Yu harmed Prince Ying of Chengdu.

units.zh: 十一月庚午，帝崩于顯陽殿，時年四十八，葬太陽陵。
units.en: He died in the Xianyang Hall on gengwu in the eleventh month at forty-eight sui and was buried at Taiyang mausoleum.
units.literal: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month the emperor died in the Xianyang Hall at forty-eight sui of age and was buried at Taiyang Mausoleum.

units.zh: 帝之爲太子也，朝廷咸知不堪政事，武帝亦疑焉。
units.en: Even as heir apparent the whole court knew he could not govern, and Emperor Wu harbored the same doubt.
units.literal: When he was crown prince, the whole court knew he could not manage government, and Emperor Wu also doubted it.

units.zh: 嘗悉召東宮官屬，使以尚書事令太子決之，帝不能對。
units.en: When Eastern Palace officials tested him with secretariat cases, he could not answer.
units.literal: Once he summoned all the Eastern Palace staff and had them present secretariat business for the crown prince to decide; the emperor could not answer.

units.zh: 賈妃遣左右代對，多引古義。
units.en: Lady Jia had her people feed him answers full of classical tags.
units.literal: Consort Jia had her attendants answer in his place, citing many classical precedents.

units.zh: 給事張泓曰：「太子不學，陛下所知。
units.en: Attendant Zhang Hong said, “Your Majesty knows the heir does not study;
units.literal: Attendant Zhang Hong said, “The crown prince does not study—this Your Majesty knows.

units.zh: 今宜以事斷，不可引書。」
units.en: he should be judged on practical matters, not book learning.”
units.literal: Now matters should be decided by affairs and cannot cite books.”

units.zh: 妃從之。
units.en: Lady Jia agreed.
units.literal: The consort followed this.

units.zh: 泓乃具草，令帝書之。
units.en: Zhang Hong drafted replies for the heir to copy.
units.literal: Hong then prepared a draft and ordered the emperor to copy it.

units.zh: 武帝覽而大悅，太子遂安。
units.en: Emperor Wu read the copies with delight, and the heir’s position was saved.
units.literal: Emperor Wu read them and was greatly pleased; the crown prince was thereby secured.

units.zh: 及居大位，政出群下，綱紀大壞，貨賂公行，勢位之家，以貴陵物，忠賢路絕，讒邪得志，更相薦舉，天下謂之互市焉。
units.en: On the throne power passed to favorites, law collapsed, offices were sold, great houses trampled commoners, honest men were shut out, flatterers traded posts, and the realm called it mutual barter.
units.literal: When he occupied the great throne, government issued from his inferiors; great order was ruined; bribes walked openly; families of power and position, relying on nobility, trampled others; paths for the loyal and worthy were cut off; slanderers and evil men got their will, recommending one another in turn; all under Heaven called it “mutual marketing.”

units.zh: 高平王沈作釋時論，南陽魯褒作錢神論，廬江杜嵩作任子春秋，皆疾時之作也。
units.en: Wang Chen, Lu Bao, and Du Song wrote satires that scourged the age.
units.literal: Wang Chen of Gaoping wrote “Explaining the Times”; Lu Bao of Nanyang wrote “The God of Cash”; Du Song of Lujiang wrote “The Sons of Office, Spring and Autumn”—all were works that railed at the age.

units.zh: 帝又嘗在華林園，聞蝦蟆聲，謂左右曰：「此鳴者爲官乎，私乎？」
units.en: In Hualin Garden he heard frogs and asked those beside him, “Do those that croak hold office, or are they private?”
units.literal: The emperor once was in the Hualin Garden, heard frogs croak, and said to those at his side, “Do those that croak hold office, or are they private?”

units.zh: 或對曰：「在官地爲官，在私地爲私。」
units.en: A courtier answered, “Those on official land are officials; those on private land are private.”
units.literal: Someone answered, “Those on official land are official; those on private land are private.”

units.zh: 及天下荒亂，百姓餓死，帝曰：「何不食肉糜？」
units.en: When famine emptied the roads he asked why the hungry did not eat meat porridge.
units.literal: When all under Heaven was desolate in chaos and commoners starved to death, the emperor said, “Why do they not eat minced meat?”

units.zh: 其蒙蔽皆此類也。
units.en: Such was the fog in which he lived.
units.literal: His benightedness was of this kind.

units.zh: 後因食䴵中毒而崩，或云司馬越之鴆。
units.en: He later died of poisoned cakes—some blamed Prince Sima Yue.
units.literal: Later he died of poisoning from eating bing; some say it was Prince Sima Yue’s poisoned cup.

units.zh: 史臣曰：不才之子，則天稱大，權非帝出，政邇宵人。
units.en: The annalist writes: Heaven loomed vast over an unworthy son; the scepter never rested in his hands; petty men held the state.
units.literal: The historian says: For an unworthy son, Heaven is called great; power did not issue from the emperor; government fell to petty men.

units.zh: 褒姒共叔帶並興，襄后與犬戎俱運。
units.en: As Bao Si and Prince Dai of the Gong line once together unhinged the Zhou house, so the queen of Xiang and the Dog Rong brought parallel disaster.
units.literal: Bao Si and Gongshu Dai rose together; the queen of Xiang and the Dog Rong moved in the same turn.

units.zh: 昔者，丹朱不肖，赧王逃責，相彼凶德，事關休咎，方乎土梗，以墜其情。
units.en: Dan Zhu’s folly and King Nan’s flight show how vicious temperaments, no stronger than clay idols, still decide weal and woe.
units.literal: In olden times Dan Zhu was unworthy; the King of Nan fled his debt; look at those vicious natures—events hinge on fortune and misfortune—compared to clay puppets, they let passion drag them down.

units.zh: 溽暑之氣將闌，淫鼃之音罕記，乃彰嗤笑，用符顛隕。
units.en: When summer’s damp heat lifted, the croak of greedy frogs faded—only mockery marked the fall.
units.literal: When the sweltering summer’s breath was about to end, the sound of lewd frogs was scarcely remembered—then ridicule was revealed, matching the overturning.

units.zh: 豈通才俊彥猶形于前代，增淫助虐獨擅于當今者歟？
units.en: Were wise men only found in antiquity while today’s court bred aides to cruelty alone?
units.literal: How could it be that penetrating talents and outstanding men appeared in former ages, while those who increased debauchery and aided cruelty monopolized the present alone?

units.zh: 物號忠良，于茲拔本，人稱祅孽，自此疏源。
units.en: Loyalty was only a label while roots rotted; men were called demons while poison welled from the same spring.
units.literal: Creatures were labeled loyal and good—here their roots were torn up; men were called portents of evil—from this their springs were parted.

units.zh: 長樂不祥，承華非命，生靈版蕩，社稷丘墟。
units.en: Changle brought no blessing, Chenghua an untimely end; the people were cast adrift and the altars lay in ruins.
units.literal: Changle proved ill-omened; Chenghua met unnatural death; living souls were scattered; altars of soil and grain became mounds and ruins.

units.zh: 古者敗國亡身，分鑣共軫，不有亂常，則多庸暗。
units.en: Ancient falls came from riot or from mediocrity.
units.literal: In old times ruined states and lost persons shared reins and traces—if it was not constant turmoil, then it was mostly mediocrity and dimness.

units.zh: 豈明神喪其精魄，武皇不知其子也！
units.en: Did the spirits desert him, or did Emperor Wu simply fail to know his child?
units.literal: How could the bright spirits have lost their essence-souls—did not Emperor Wu know his own son?

units.zh: 贊曰：惠皇居尊，臨朝聽言。
units.en: The encomium: Kind Hui held the throne and heard petitions.
units.literal: The eulogy says: The Kind Emperor sat in honor and listened to court from the throne.

units.zh: 厥體斯昧，其情則昏。
units.en: His mind was dim, his judgment dark.
units.literal: His substance was thus dim; his disposition was thus dark.

units.zh: 高臺望子，長夜奚冤。
units.en: He watched from a tower for an heir through endless unjust nights.
units.literal: From a high terrace he watched for a son; through long nights what wrong could be righted?

units.zh: 金墉毀冕，蕩陰釋冑。
units.en: Crown princes perished at Jinyong; armor was shed in blood at Dangyin.
units.literal: The crown was shattered at Jinyong; armor was cast off at Dangyin.

units.zh: 及爾皆亡，滔天來遘。
units.en: When all was lost, Heaven’s deluge closed over him.
units.literal: When you reached that end, Heaven’s flood came to meet you.

units.zh: 校勘記
units.en: Editorial collation section.
units.literal: Textual collation notes.

units.zh: 永平元年 是年三月又改元「元康」，依例應作「元康元年」。
units.en: The note argues that after the third-month rename the text should read “Yuankang first year,” not “Yongping first year.”
units.literal: Yongping first year: In the third month of that year the era name was again changed to “Yuankang”; by rule it ought to read “Yuankang first year.”

units.zh: 此仍作「永平」，則三月改元後應出「元康」年號，使讀者明白自此以下至九年皆「元康之年」。
units.en: Because it still reads “Yongping” here, the chronicle should insert the “Yuankang” era after the rename so readers know everything down to the ninth year belongs to Yuankang.
units.literal: Because it still reads “Yongping” here, after the third-month change the text ought to give the “Yuankang” era so readers know everything down to the ninth year belongs to Yuankang.

units.zh: 紀文此處既用「永平」，下文又不出「元康」，似自此至九年皆屬「永平」矣。
units.en: Since the text uses “Yongping” here and never introduces “Yuankang” below, it seems as if down to the ninth year everything were still “Yongping.”
units.literal: Since the text uses “Yongping” here and never introduces “Yuankang” below, it seems as if down to the ninth year everything were still Yongping.

units.zh: 此爲史例之失。
units.en: The compilers call this a flaw in annalistic practice.
units.literal: This is a lapse in historiographical convention.

units.zh: 五月甲戌 五月癸未朔，此「甲戌」及下「壬午」均在四月，「五月」二字疑衍。
units.en: The collation doubts “fifth month” before jiaxu and renwu.
units.literal: Fifth month jiaxu: Fifth month guimao new moon—this “jiaxu” and the following “renwu” both fall in the fourth month; the characters “fifth month” are probably redundant.

units.zh: 太原王泓薨 本書太原成王輔傳「泓」作「弘」。
units.en: The annals write the princely name as “Hong” with the water radical, while the biography of Prince Cheng of Taiyuan uses “Hong” with the sun radical.
units.literal: Prince Hong of Taiyuan died: In the biography of Prince Cheng of Taiyuan in this book, the character read hong with the water radical is written hong with the sun radical.

units.zh: 且弘時已改中丘王。
units.en: The prince had already been moved to the Zhongqiu title.
units.literal: Moreover Hong had by then been transferred to prince of Zhongqiu.

units.zh: 安昌公石鑒薨 《通鑑考異》：本傳封昌安縣侯。
units.en: Duke Shi Jian of Anchang died. Zizhi tongjian kaoyi notes that his biography enfeoffs him as Marquis of Chang’an County.
units.literal: Duke Shi Jian of Anchang died: Tongjian kaoyi: his biography enfeoffs him as marquis of Chang’an county.

units.zh: 斠注：以石
units.en: A truncated collation gloss citing evidence about the Shi surname breaks off mid-sentence in the received text.
units.literal: Collation note: with Shi

units.zh: 〈其少〉、
units.en: 〈A damaged bracketed gloss whose surviving words mean roughly 'its lesser [remainder lost]' is preserved in the collation.〉
units.literal: 〈Its lesser〉

units.zh: 石定二墓碣證之，「安昌」當作「昌安」。
units.en: Epitaphs for two men surnamed Shi, including Shi Ding, show that “Anchang” is a scribal transposition and should read “Changan.”
units.literal: The tomb inscriptions of Shi Ding and a second Shi man prove it; the place-name Anchang should be emended to Changan.
